key_insight: POEM-CMA makes zeroth-order optimization more efficient by adapting its sampling covariance to the problem’s geometry and replacing ambient dimension with an effective dimension estimate.
engineering_relevance: This is useful for black-box engineering optimization where gradients are unavailable, especially when the objective has low-rank or anisotropic structure.
method: Builds a covariance matrix from gradient estimates to sample search directions anisotropically.
Uses empirical effective dimension d* = tr(Σ̂)/λ_max(Σ̂) in sampling and complexity.
Remains parameter-free while targeting near-optimal stochastic zeroth-order query complexity.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experiments on hinge-loss binary classification with LibSVM datasets, showing better performance than the original POEM, especially when d* ≪ d.
watch_item: Performance depends on estimating covariance/gradient structure reliably, so noisy or poorly conditioned problems may reduce the benefit of the adaptive sampling.
paper_title: A Parameter-Free Zeroth-Order Method with Covariance Matrix Adaptation and Effective Dimension
